alternative: Accuracy, not RL's directions. On hard328 the 1.5x edit and RL plain are about equally accurate (per sample 200.25 vs 200.0 of 328; 14.3 % vs 15.5 % on base-0/4 problems), and both are well above the cued base (about 164). A more accurate model gets rid of the base's careless, one-off wrong values: long arithmetic slips and wrong values that finish after loops. Its remaining finished wrong answers are the systematic near-misses that any strong solver reaches (a missed case, a misread condition), and these are the values RL's wrong answers also land on. On the same problems, the per-problem weighting of cross pairs (w_X * w_R) also lines up with the within-pair weighting when X's wrong counts track RL's, and the normalization rewards that alignment. So any model with RL-level accuracy and no RL weights should give a positive N(X,R) - N(B,R) of the same size. The test: Think-SFT + cue is accuracy-matched (209.0 of 328 per sample against the edit's 200.25 and RL's 200.0), carries no RL weight change and no RL edit, and has 4 attempt-0 samples stored on hard328. Its normalized wrong-answer agreement with RL, minus the cued base's, should land at about +0.1 to +0.2, inside [0.08, 0.6].
computation: 1) From studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01 (rows.jsonl), take Think-SFT + cue attempt-0 samples 0-3 on hard328. Keep its finished wrong answers by the consequence's rule: v3 wrong, not a cap hit (16,384 cap), extracted answer present. Call this model T. 2) From studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01 (R) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01 (B), take the finished wrong attempt-0 samples 0-3 with the same rule. 3) Rows: the hard328 problems where T, R and B each have at least 1 finished wrong answer. Within pairs come from the problems among these where the model has at least 2. 4) Two answers agree when math-verify 0.9.0 judges them equal. Pooled over the rows, compute A(T,R) and A(B,R) = agreeing cross pairs / all cross pairs, and A(T,T), A(B,B), A(R,R) = agreeing within pairs / all within pairs. 5) N(T,R) = A(T,R)/sqrt(A(T,T)*A(R,R)) and N(B,R) = A(B,R)/sqrt(A(B,B)*A(R,R)). 6) The alternative's predicted value of D is D_T = N(T,R) - N(B,R), one unitless number on the statistic's scale. If fewer than 50 problems qualify, use the problems where T and R each have at least 1 finished wrong answer and B's pooled A's from the consequence's own rows.
